archetypes.name: doc-scope-audit
archetypes.rationale: Plan updates only 2 contract .md files but other docs describing git-archive restore (pause/SKILL.md, workflow-lifecycle.md, design-pause-save.md) may also carry stale language that will drift from the new ls-tree+show implementation.
archetypes.prompt_body: The plan touches `scripts/design-log-publish.md` and `scripts/design-pause-load.md` but does not audit whether other docs reference the old `git archive | tar` restore mechanism or the old marker-deletion-on-failure behavior. Check `skills/pause/SKILL.md`, `docs/workflow-lifecycle.md`, any other canonical sources listed in AGENTS.md (docs/issue-anchored-plan.md, docs/run-logs.md) and `scripts/design-pause-save.md` for mentions of git archive, export-ignore, or the delete-on-failure marker contract. If any of those files describe the old behavior but are absent from the plan's file list, that is a missing-scope defect. Also flag the duplicated paragraph in the plan's `design-pause-load.md` section (lines 28-30 appear verbatim again at lines 30-31) as a possible inconsistency. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: allowlist-source-verification
archetypes.rationale: Plan hardcodes 4 driver phase names (emit_plan, tally, finalize, validate_plan_commands) into design-log-publish.sh, but design-driver.sh is absent from scope-files and the plan never instructs a grep verification — the list could be stale or incomplete.
archetypes.prompt_body: The plan's WI1 fix introduces an explicit 4-name allowlist (`emit_plan`, `tally`, `finalize`, `validate_plan_commands`) into `scripts/design-log-publish.sh`, claiming these are the current action names written by `skills/design/scripts/design-driver.sh`. Verify this claim by reading `design-driver.sh` and checking what values are actually passed to the sentinel-write logic (`$DESIGN_TMPDIR/.completed/$step_name`). If the real action names differ from the 4 listed, or if there are additional action names not in the allowlist, the WI1 fix will still fail at runtime. Also check whether `normalize_step` lowercasing is applied before the sentinel write (the plan asserts lowercased names, but if the driver writes mixed-case names the allowlist would need adjustment). Finally, confirm whether `design-route.sh` or any caller of `design-driver.sh` writes its own `.completed/` sentinels outside the driver, which the plan silently omits. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: marker-refactor-completeness
archetypes.rationale: WI3 removes the delete-parameter from emit_load_fail and all its call sites inside design-pause-load.sh, but the plan enumerates call sites by category rather than exhaustive list, leaving open whether any callers outside that file also pass the now-dropped boolean argument.
archetypes.prompt_body: The WI3 refactor drops the `${2:-false}` delete parameter from `emit_load_fail` and strips all `true` arguments from its call sites. The plan lists ~7 call-site categories but does not show an exhaustive enumeration from a grep. Read `scripts/design-pause-load.sh` to count every actual `emit_load_fail` invocation and check that none are missed; also grep the broader repo for any other script that sources or calls `emit_load_fail` or `clear_pause_marker` — if either helper is defined in a shared library sourced by other scripts, callers outside `design-pause-load.sh` may silently break. Separately, verify that the plan's instruction to drop `|| true` from the post-success `clear_pause_marker` call is unambiguous: if `clear_pause_marker` is itself a function defined locally in the script (not an external binary), check whether its internal exit-path logic is already unconditional or whether removing `|| true` could surface a previously swallowed non-zero from a different failure mode than the intended marker-write race. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
